subject: Re: Accelerator credit stacking with Marketplace SKU — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightbridge.vc>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightbridge.vc
Date: 2027-06-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Accelerator credits — can they stack with Marketplace SKU credits?

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking a look. Quick question from our side as we finalize the BrightBridge accelerator package: we receive a set of Redwood promo credits for cohort members (noted in the attached promo_terms). A few of our founders are also on the AWS Marketplace and inquired whether the Redwood Marketplace SKU credits (applied by AWS billing) can be stacked with the cohort promo credits — specifically, whether both can be applied to the same consumption without double-counting.

High level ask: is there a way to split credits so that founders can use cohort promo credits for experimentation while we convert a portion into a reserved-capacity discount for teams that signal production intent? If yes, what gating / paperwork do you need? We have a narrow window to finalize onboarding materials this week.

Attaching the cohort promo terms for context (brightbridge_promo_terms.pdf).

Appreciate any guidance — cc'ed our legal team for visibility.

Thanks,
Hannah Lowe
Community Director — BrightBridge Ventures
H: 415-555-0124

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightbridge.vc>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator credits — can they stack with Marketplace SKU credits?

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Short answer: yes, we can support a split approach, but we need to avoid any double-counting on the billing side and confirm routing for the Marketplace SKU usage. A few constraints up front:

- We cannot allow the same token/usage line to be claimed twice.
- Marketplace-applied discounts are handled at the cloud billing layer; promo credits in our system are applied on top of that only when we can verify usage attribution.

Here's a pragmatic proposal for BrightBridge founders that keeps things simple for founders and accounting teams:

1) Allow up to 50% of cohort promo credits to be converted to a Reserved-Capacity credit (applied as a Redwood invoice credit / discount) for teams that commit to a 6–12 month reserved instance.
2) The remaining 50% remains as on-account promo credits in the hosted API (usable for experimentation).
3) For any Marketplace-billed usage, we require the founder to opt-in to Marketplace billing (so AWS applies the SKU discount). We will then mark that usage as Marketplace-attributed and exclude it from promo-credit chargebacks to prevent double-counting.

Next steps we need from your side:
- List of founding companies that want the conversion (simple spreadsheet)
- Confirmation whether the Marketplace SKU flows through AWS consolidated billing (yes/no)
- A signed addendum per account that authorizes Redwood to convert part of the promo credits to an invoice discount (we can send a DocuSign).

Ben / Laura — looping you in to confirm whether finance/legal are OK with the 50/50 split and the conversion mechanics. I attached a draft MAP (redwood_map_draft.pdf) for internal ops notes.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightbridge.vc>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator credits — follow-up with conversion numbers

Thanks Olga — agree with the approach. To make the offer concrete for founders, here is a proposed allocation we can communicate in the BrightBridge onboarding doc: 

- Standard cohort credit = $10,000 consumption credit per company.
- Conversion option at onboarding: convert up to $6,000 (60%) of that credit into a Reserved-Capacity credit that maps to a month-by-month invoice discount if the founder signs a 12-month reserved commit at $1,200/mo net.
- The remaining $4,000 (40%) stays as on-account promo credits for hosted/testing usage and will not be convertible later.

Rationale: a slightly skewed split (60/40) gives founders enough runway to prove production signals while still leaving experimentation credit. It also maps cleanly to our reserved SKU tiers. If finance/legal prefers 50/50, we can swap easily.

Operational asks:
- If we convert credits to invoice discounts we need a simple SOW addendum per account and a HubSpot deal stage update.
- I will prepare a two-row CSV (company, conversion_amount) for ops once we get sign-offs.

Hannah — if that allocation works, we can put this in the onboarding card and send the DocuSign link.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0172
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightbridge.vc>
Date: 2027-06-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator credits — finance/legal check

Ben / Olga — quick finance/legal notes:

- We can support the credit conversion but need each converted amount to be attached to an SOW amendment that includes: effective dates, billing entity, and tax treatment.
- For Marketplace SKU usage: we need consolidated-billing confirmation from the founder/org so our systems can reconcile against AWS usage exports. Without that, we cannot mark usage as Marketplace-attributed and must treat consumption as billable against promo credits.
- Please add the following to the DocuSign: a checkbox where founder confirms consolidated billing and specifies the AWS account id(s).

I attached a short accounting note (accting_note.pdf) — it outlines revenue recognition implications and the minimum data we require from the customer (invoice routing, commitment term).

If BrightBridge agrees to the SOW addendum + consolidated billing confirmation, finance signs off.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Ops & Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightbridge.vc>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator credits — next steps and DocuSign

Hi Hannah — thanks, all. We have internal alignment: finance requires the SOW addendum + AWS consolidated billing confirmation. Ben's proposed split (60% conversion / 40% on-account) is acceptable if BrightBridge is comfortable with that ratio; otherwise we can default to the 50/50 Olga-proposal.

I've prepared the DocuSign addendum (link below) which includes the AWS account id checkbox and the conversion amount field per company. Please get the founders to complete the CSV and sign the addendum by EOD Thursday so we can process conversions in the June billing cycle.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/sign/ABC12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/BRIDGE-342

If you'd like, we can run a 20-minute ops walkthrough for your cohort managers to explain how the conversion shows up on both the marketplace bill and the founder's Redwood invoice.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_map_draft.pdf
